title: Affine-line support classes: finite-Tor realization and exceptional transpose
statement:
Fix the finite purity datum [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, assume $e=e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$, and put $N=n/e\geq1$ and $m=\ell^N$, so $mA=0$. Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. In the affine-line datum [def-pur-affine-line-datum] write $X=\mathbf A^1_Y$, $s:Y\hookrightarrow X$ for the zero section, $U=\mathbf G_{m,Y}$ for its complement, $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and $F=A_X(1)$. The coefficient comparison is $\theta_T:A_T(1)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{m,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/m}A$, and $\varphi_T(u)=\theta_T^{-1}(u\otimes1_A)$.

Use small etale and pro-etale sites, supported cohomology [def-pur-support-cohomology], finite Tor amplitude and its full category $D^b_{ctf}$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and the transported exceptional functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. There is an integer $d\geq0$ bounding $\dim X$, with $d=0$ allowed if $X$ is empty; $j$ is quasi-compact and $(U,X)$ satisfies the ordinary etale open-complement condition [def-exc-open-complement-bound] with $c=2d$. The etale closed direct image has an ambient right adjoint $Rs_e^!$ without any open-complement hypothesis. This adjoint preserves bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude under the stated condition. The etale model $F_e=\mu_{m,X}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/m}A$ and $F=\nu_X^*F_e$ are locally constant finite rank-one $A$-sheaves with Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. Both $A_Y$ and $K=Rs^!F[2]$ belong to $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, and $K$ is concentrated in degree zero.

Let $\chi:H^2_{s(Y)}(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(s_*A_Y,F[2])$ be the supported-Hom identification [lem-pur-supported-hom]. For every $\alpha\in H^2_{s(Y)}(X,F)$ there is a unique morphism $u_\alpha:A_Y\to K$ whose degree-zero section under the Gysin identification [lem-pur-gysin-structure] corresponds to $\alpha$. With $\varepsilon:s_*K\to F[2]$ the exceptional counit on etale-origin objects, the identifications agree by
$$\chi(\alpha)=\varepsilon\circ s_*u_\alpha.$$
In particular, for $\alpha=\partial\kappa(t)$, where $\partial$ is the support boundary [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] and $\kappa(t)$ is the datum's coefficient-extended Kummer class, the degree-zero sheaf map of $u_\alpha$ sends $1$ to the section corresponding to $\partial\kappa(t)$. All morphisms here are obtained from their ordinary etale models by the site comparison; no adjunction on all pro-etale complexes is asserted.

proof.text: By [lem-pur-zero-support-retraction-triangle], $A$ is finite, $X,U,Y$ are Noetherian and finite type over $k$, and $j$ is quasi-compact. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] choose a finite integer $d\geq0$ bounding $\dim X$; take $d=0$ when $X$ is empty. The coefficient-level statement [lem-pur-finite-kummer-level] gives $\ell^NA=0$. Thus [lem-exc-open-complement-known] applies to $(U,X,A)$ and gives precisely the two open-complement conditions with $c=2d$.

source.place: Ambient qualifications; verification of the finite-dimensional closed/open pair.

proof.text: Apply [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] with exponent $m$, invertible on $X$, and $mA=0$: $F_e=\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{m,X}\otimes A$ is a locally constant finite rank-one flat $A$-sheaf. The pro-etale line has the same properties by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](1),(3), with the coefficient identification of [lem-pur-finite-kummer-level]. The comparison $\nu_X^*F_e=F$ is the roots-and-tensor comparison of the affine-line datum, with its local formula also on $X$: on a trivializing etale cover choose a primitive root $\zeta$; both roots sheaves are trivialized by $a\mapsto\zeta^a$, and both tensor lines by $\zeta^a\otimes b\mapsto ab$. On an overlap $\zeta'=\zeta^v$, both formulas change by the same multiplication by $v$, hence glue and identify $u\otimes1$ with $\varphi_X(u)$. Exact comparison preserves the constant coefficient sheaf by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Locally tensor with either line is tensor with $A$, hence exact; its degree-zero flat representative has Tor interval $[0,0]$. The constant $A_Y$ has the same interval since $A_Y\otimes_A^LM=M$; its single constant finite stratum makes it constructible. Thus $A_Y\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$.

source.place: Finite coefficient and site refinements of the twist input; local trivializations from the affine-line datum.

proof.text: The ambient ordinary etale adjoint $Rs_e^!$ exists by [lem-exc-closed-ambient], independently of step 1's open-complement bound. Under that bound [lem-exc-closed-amplitude] sends a bounded constructible interval $[a,b]$ into $[a,b+2d+1]$, and [prop-exc-closed-tor] gives that same interval as a Tor bound for a bounded constructible input of Tor interval $[a,b]$. This proves the claimed preservation on the etale site without confusing bounded constructibility with finite Tor amplitude.

source.place: Ambient etale existence and preservation qualifications.

proof.text: Put $B_0=Rs_0^!F$, the classical support value. The triangle in [lem-pur-zero-support-retraction-triangle] has second arrow exactly derived restriction, so [lem-pur-kummer-triangle-concentration] applies and supplies a derived isomorphism $A_Y[0]\cong C_0=B_0[2]$, with $C_0\in D^b_{ctf}$ and no cohomology outside degree zero. Its stated hypotheses are the original affine-line datum, not a purity isomorphism to be proved. Apply [lem-pur-supported-class-evaluation-comparison] to $i=s$ and input $F$: step 1 verifies the finite-type closed pair and quasi-compact complement, while the preceding isomorphism verifies both hypotheses on $C_0$. It gives $\phi[2]:C_0\cong K=Rs^!F[2]$, preserving concentration and finite-Tor constructibility, and gives isomorphisms $\eta:H^2_{s(Y)}(X,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A_Y,K)$ and $\mathrm{ev}:\operatorname{Hom}(A_Y,K)\cong\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H^0K)$.

source.place: Localization and concentration, followed by the counit-normalized support/exceptional identification.

proof.text: For every $\alpha$ define $u_\alpha=\eta(\alpha)$. The evaluation comparison states that $(\mathrm{ev}\eta)^{-1}$ is the canonical section-to-support identification; this is the Gysin identification of [lem-pur-gysin-structure]. It follows that the section of $u_\alpha$ corresponds to $\alpha$, and uniqueness follows from the bijectivity of $\mathrm{ev}$ and $\eta$. More explicitly, the formula for $\eta$ in [lem-pur-supported-class-evaluation-comparison] is $\chi$ of [lem-pur-supported-hom], followed by support adjunction, shifts, and $\phi[2]$. That lemma identifies this with the relative exceptional adjunction. The inverse adjunct of $u_\alpha$ is therefore $\varepsilon\circ s_*u_\alpha$; applying the inverse bijection to $\eta(\alpha)$ gives exactly $\chi(\alpha)=\varepsilon\circ s_*u_\alpha$. This fixes the counit and shift normalization, rather than choosing an arbitrary isomorphism of the two Hom groups.

source.place: Second paragraph: the supported Hom isomorphism and degree-zero section identification.

proof.text:
All the maps just used have ordinary etale representatives. Indeed step 2 gives $F=
u_X^*F_e$, and the ambient etale adjoint value of $F_e$ is bounded below by step 3. Full faithfulness of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] identifies maps between these etale-origin objects, including every $u_\alpha$, with their unique etale maps. The more precise statement [lem-coef-site-closed-counit-transport], with $H=F_e[2]$, $i=s$ and $L=A_Y$, gives $E\,s_*(\alpha_H)\,\delta_{IH}=
u_X^*(e_H)$ and identifies the transported adjunct of an etale map with $\alpha_H
u_Y^*(\widehat f)$. Its finite-field, separated finite-type and bounded-below hypotheses hold by the datum and steps 1-3. Hence the equation of step 5 uses exactly the etale counit transported by the canonical closed direct-image comparison. The exact comparison commutes with the displayed shifts. This proves the site-origin qualification without extending the adjunction to arbitrary pro-etale inputs.

source.place: Final site-comparison sentence, restricted to etale-origin objects and the specified counit.

proof.text: Finally [def-pur-affine-line-datum] defines the coefficient-extended class $\kappa(t)$ on $U$, and [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] gives $\partial\kappa(t)\in H^2_{s(Y)}(X,F)$. Substitute this class for $\alpha$ in step 5. Evaluation is explicitly $u\mapsto\mathcal H^0(u)(1)$ by [lem-pur-supported-class-evaluation-comparison]; thus its degree-zero sheaf map sends $1$ to the section corresponding to $\partial\kappa(t)$, as required.
